text: Can you look up the paper 'BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding' and give me the APA citation for it?
label: search_papers -> format_citation
rationale: The student gives only the title. format_citation needs an arXiv id, which is unknown until search_papers returns 1810.04805; the second call's argument is read from the first call's result, so a single round with no id would have to guess.

text: How many citations does 'LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models' have on Semantic Scholar?
label: search_papers -> get_citation_count
rationale: get_citation_count takes an arXiv id, not a title. The agent must first search for the title to obtain 2106.09685 and only then query the count with that id. In Stage 4 the single tool round ends after the search and the count is never fetched.

text: Which one is cited more, 'LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models' or 'Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models'? Give me both numbers.
label: search_papers (x2) -> get_citation_count (x2)
rationale: Two titles, no ids. The agent needs search_papers for each title (2302.13971 and 2307.09288), and only after both ids are known can it call get_citation_count twice and compare. The searches can run in parallel, but the counts cannot be requested in the same round as the searches.

text: I wrote down arXiv 2210.03629 in my notes but I forgot what it is. Can you tell me what the paper is about and then find me 3 other papers on the same topic?
label: get_paper -> search_papers
rationale: The search query (ReAct, reasoning and acting, LLM agents) is only known after get_paper returns the title and abstract for 2210.03629. The student never names the topic, so search_papers cannot be planned in the first round.

text: Find papers about language model agents that reason and use tools, tell me which one is the most cited, and give me the BibTeX for that one.
label: search_papers -> get_citation_count (xN) -> format_citation
rationale: Three dependent hops: the candidate ids (ReAct 2210.03629, Toolformer 2302.04761, Reflexion 2303.11366, Tree of Thoughts 2305.10601) come from the search, the counts need those ids, and format_citation can only be called once the comparison picks a winner. Each step's input is the previous step's output.

text: In my thesis draft I cited 'Generative Adversarial Networks' by Goodfellow, 2016. Is that correct? If something is wrong, fix it and give me the correct BibTeX entry.
label: check_citation -> search_papers -> format_citation
rationale: check_citation reports that the year is wrong (the paper is from 2014) but returns no arXiv id, so the agent must search for the paper to get 1406.2661 and then call format_citation. Whether the second and third calls happen at all depends on what the first call reports, so the path cannot be fixed in advance.

text: Who is the second author on 'Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer'? And does that person have any other papers in this collection?
label: search_papers -> search_papers
rationale: The second search is an author query whose argument (Noam Shazeer) is unknown until the first search returns the author list for 1910.10683. The agent cannot form the second query without reading the first result (it should then find 1706.03762).

text: I'm doing a related-work section on transformers for computer vision. Can you find the relevant papers in the collection and give me BibTeX entries for all of them?
label: search_papers -> format_citation (xN)
rationale: format_citation needs one arXiv id per paper (2010.11929 ViT and 2103.00020 CLIP are the matches in the cache), and the set of ids only exists after the search returns. Even the number of format_citation calls depends on how many results come back.

text: A reviewer flagged my reference 'Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning' by Yao, 2023. Can you check whether that reference is right, and also tell me how many citations the paper has so I know whether to keep it?
label: check_citation -> search_papers -> get_citation_count
rationale: Wrong FIRST AUTHOR this time (Shunyu Yao is the last author of 2303.11366; Noah Shinn is first), so check_citation reports the author mismatch; the agent then needs the id (search_papers) before get_citation_count can run. Three dependent calls.

text: Here's an id from a lecture slide: 1301.3781. What is this paper, and can you find the paper in the collection that's closest to it and compare their citation counts?
label: get_paper -> search_papers -> get_citation_count (x2)
rationale: The topic (word embeddings) is only known after get_paper returns the word2vec metadata; the related paper (e.g. Sentence-BERT, 1908.10084) is only known after the search; and the two citation counts need both ids. Nothing after the first call can be decided before its result arrives.

text: Give me the BibTeX for arXiv 1412.6980.
label: single
rationale: The arXiv id and the style are both given, so format_citation("1412.6980", "bibtex") answers the request in one call. Any preceding get_paper or search_papers call is unnecessary and should be counted as an extra call in the Stage 5 experiment.
